en: Oh, <Color:8>Miso Stewed Udon with Nagoya Cochin Chicken<Color:Default>! That looks delicious!
(Shion-chan's got her eye on that <Color:8>Miso Stewed Udon with Nagoya Cochin Chicken<Color:Default>.)
Do you come here often, Shinada-san?
Not really. Why do you ask?
I've wanted to come here for some time, but I didn't know anyone who could introduce me, so I wasn't afforded the opportunity.
What's wrong with coming here by yourself? That's what I've always done.
And you didn't have a letter of introduction?
A what? I don't think there are any places around here that'd need something like that.
Oh, really? I always get introduced to new establishments by my friends, and so I'd assumed this place was like that as well.
Bring your friends next time. Then you can be the one to introduce them.
Good idea! And I'll have to tell my friends all about you, Shinada-san, won't I?
About me? Uh, no, you don't have to do that.
No, I simply must! It would reflect poorly on me to not pay proper respects to the person who introduced me to this place.
It's really not that big a thing...
Making your name a topic of conversation can spread the word about you. Talking only of oneself is much too tedious and gauche.
Gau... che? Aw geez, this is another one of your fancy high society rules, isn't it?
That's a bit silly. Not many places are that picky about who comes in.
But haven't you ever been invited to a new place by the owner when it's first opened?
Oh, yeah, I guess I have! Like a new parlor will open up and they'll be all, "Hey, come on by, it's on the house!"
I guess they want to make a good impression, so I'll give them a glowing write-up and bring in more customers for them.
Precisely! By starting with people whom they trust as guests, an establishment can build a much better reputation.
I've heard stories of places that have opened to the general public first, only to have rivals send people in to cause embarrassing incidents.
Oh, wow! I know lots of places that failed pretty quickly. I didn't realize competition was so intense!
You should introduce me! I'd love to go to a place like that! Then once you've introduced me, I can go by myself, right?
I don't mind introducing you, Shinada-san, but if you go back after that, then you need to introduce another friend of your own.
What? Why?
These places earn their business through their clientele introducing new customers. If you keep coming alone, they don't make any money.
That's why it would be rude of me to introduce someone who would not continue the pattern of bringing someone new on their next visit.
Oh, I get it. Since it's so exclusive, they need people to help them grow.
If you ask me, seems like less trouble to just let everyone in to begin with.
Uncle Kaz, I'd really like some <Color:8>Miso Stewed Udon with Choice Kurobuta<Color:Default>.
(Haruka wants to have some <Color:8>Miso Stewed Udon with Choice Kurobuta<Color:Default>.)
But I wanted some <Color:8>Miso Stewed Udon with Choice Kurobuta<Color:Default>.
Thank you very much. I hope that was to your liking.
Hello, welcome! How may I help you?
Excuse me! Do you like shogi, by any chance? Are you good at it? How good?
Whoa, slow down... What is this all about?
Oh, I beg your pardon. I got a little carried away. My name is Kongoin.
I have ambitions of becoming a shogi master, but I've hit a wall. My progress has stalled.
A shogi master? You're that good? Your name sounds right for the part, at least. Though I don't see how I can help you.
Kongoin is my real name, so I didn't pick it to sound strong or anything. I've never played against a person, only computers.
Why don't you go to a shogi club or association? I don't see why you need me.
No, I couldn't... I could never do that!
If you'd never played soccer before, you wouldn't just go try out for a professional soccer team, right? It's like that.
So, I figured if I played shogi by myself, someone would come along, and I could play them. And hello, here you are. Perfect, right?
I mean, who else but a shogi fan would bother talking to a guy with a shogi board out? Sound logic, yes?
Please, just one match! All I need to build up my confidence is to play against a real, live human being! Just once, please?
Sure. Let's see how good you are.
Oh, thank you! I really appreciate it. Let's do this!
I'm afraid I don't have the time.
Oh, that's a shame. Still, I'll be here. Let me know if you change your mind!
Oh, uh, you from before! Can I get you to play shogi with me?
Wow, you're very good. Playing against a human is really different from playing against a computer.
Oh, yes. You don't play anything like the AI in Shogi for Kids!
...Glad to hear it. See you.
No, don't run off yet. Can you play me again?
What? We just played a match not thirty seconds ago.
I'm not necessarily saying right now, just sometime soon! Anytime you've got some time.
I learned so much more than ever before just by playing a real, live human. I think if I play you multiple times, I'll get real good at this game, fast!
I'll buy a new PC shogi game so I can get ready for our rematch.
So please, if you get the time, I hope you'll think of me and my shogi board.
Wait, what? I won? Thanks for letting me win. I am grateful for that, but this doesn't really help me.
I wasn't trying to let you win...
Please, I'd love to have a rematch with you, to help me achieve true mastery!
Ah, you're back! You're, uh...
Right, right, Suzuki-san. I remember! I've gotten much better since our last game.
Am I right in assuming you came back to play me again?
Yeah, that's right.
Very well. Let's get on with our match. I can't wait!
Oh my, schooled yet again. I'm sure I've improved, but playing a living opponent face to face is very different.
Still, you gave me the confidence to go to a real shogi club. But may I ask you to play one last match with me?
What? We're not done yet?
I need one last nudge of confidence. I think I told you before, but I'm hoping to become a shogi master.
Yeah, I remember that vaguely.
To succeed as a shogi player, I need my talent to emerge from its cocoon, transformed into a thing of beauty and renown!
Uh-huh... And you think playing me again will help with your... cocoon?
Absolutely! If I can play one more match against you, I'm sure my talent will come crawling out of its chrysalis as a fully-formed shogi butterfly!
...Right.
Like before, I will be waiting here for a rematch. Please come back when you get a chance!
Please, I'd love to have a rematch with you, to help my butterfly of talent emerge!
Ah, Suzuki-san! I've been waiting for you!
I actually went to a real shogi club after I saw you. They made me take a test, and they said I  was already playing at a professional level!
Is that right? Then you don't need me to play you anymore, now, do you?
Not so! Like I said before, I need to play you one last time to really find success in the world of professional shogi.
Please, I'm begging you. Just one last match to help me become a shogi master.
All right. This is it.
Excellent! Let us begin!
Wow, as masterful as ever! I thought I'd gotten a lot better, but playing a person just isn't the same.
You have gotten better, I can tell.
I'm sure I can succeed as a pro shogi player now. Watch for me in the news!
Oh, silly me, I wanted to give you this. Please accept it.
I'll see you around!
Do you happen to know why white chocolate is white, sir?
I'm guessin' because it's made with milk?
That would be milk chocolate.
All chocolate is made by fermenting the main ingredient, cocoa beans. The chocolate color comes from the cocoa mass.
This cocoa mass can be further broken down into cocoa butter and cocoa powder.
White chocolate is prepared from cocoa butter mixed with sugar and milk, but without cocoa mass. That's why it's colored white.
So it's all made from the same stuff.
Indeed. However, in addition to lacking the bitter cocoa mass, the addition of sugar and milk makes it far sweeter than normal chocolate.
(So that's why white chocolate is white. I could bring that up at the cabaret club.)
Thank you for coming in.
Ooh, aren't you a little sweetheart? Sweet as you are, I can't serve anyone under age. You're welcome to come back in a few years though, darling!
Oh, hello. Are you ready to order?
Sorry, but you've had too many already. That's enough, all right?
Can I interest you in another?
Oh. Is that so? Come again.
Uh-oh, you're not of age, are you? I'm sorry, but we can't serve you here. We'd love to have you back when you're legal.
Welcome. Have you decided what you want?
(I don't need a taxi right now. Besides, I shouldn't waste money.)
Would you like to go to Tsukimino? That'll be 650 yen.
Would you like to go back to Kineicho?
Hello. I can exchange your pachinko balls and slots tokens for prizes. Which would you like to exchange?
Hi. I'll exchange your slot machine tokens for prizes.
You can trade in your tags for prizes here. Anything catch your eye?
Sure. Drop by when you rake in some tags.
We'll need you to buy wooden tags if you want to play here. How many would you like? One tag is 100 yen.
I'll take 50 tags.
All right! Have yourself a good time.
I'll take 100 tags.
I'll take 1,000 tags.
No thanks. Not now.
Oh yeah? Well, maybe pick some up next time.
Hey, you don't have enough to pay for that! Come back when you got money.
Thanks for comin', Haruka-chan! Let's get back to auditioning for the show!
Thanks for comin', Haruka-chan! Let's go audition again. We gotta clear the second round!
We got some free time for now. Let's meet back here again later.
Like I told ya, next up is the final round. We've come this far, so I really wanna see it through till the end with ya, Haruka-chan.
It'd be awesome if you could help me out one last time. Sorry to keep askin' so much of ya, Haruka-chan.
Oh, don't worry about it. It's been a great experience.
I really appreciate ya sayin' that. There's still time to spare before the final round, so lemme know when you're ready.
I just need your help for one last round!
Thanks for comin', Haruka-chan! It's time for the final round! Let's go do this!
I'm ready! Let's give it our all!
Thanks for comin', Haruka-chan! Let's take another crack at the audition! We gotta see if we can pass the final round this time!
Okay! Let's do our best!
I been thinking, Haruka-chan. What would ya say to carryin' on as my partner?
We got real chemistry as a team, and passin' this audition's bound to get us gigs on other TV shows, too.
Haruo! There ya are!
Akihiko! What's up? I thought ya found yourself a job.
Yeah, but I changed my mind.
I went to the job interview, but I pulled out at the last minute.
They asked me what my goal was. I had a good, hard think about that one. What is it I really want outta life?
After 'bout three minutes of the ol' gears turnin', I told 'em all I wanna do is conquer the comedy world, then I up and left.
Man...
Sorry for what I did to ya, Haruo. I realized I really do wanna do comedy with ya. Will ya team up with me again?
Come on! We'll crush it together!
Congratulations on getting the team back together!
Huh? Who's this cutie?
My name is Haruka-chan. Nice to meet you. I'm one of Haruo's fans.
For real!? That's awesome!
I'll be rooting for you, Haruo. I know one day you're going to rock the comedy world.
Yeah... Yeah!
I guess comedians and pop idols live in two different worlds. We gotta walk our own paths.
What're ya talkin' about? Idols?
Nah, never mind.
Anyway, whatever! We're a team again. Let's make this happen!
Thanks, Haruo!
I guess this is goodbye, Haruka-chan. Maybe we'll run into each other on a TV show someday.

This's your share of the audition prize money.
Take it, Haruka-chan.
You got <Color:8>50,000 yen<Color:Default>.
Thank you. This was a great experience for me. Comedy is pretty interesting. I'd love to give it another shot sometime.
Glad to hear it! Oh, yeah. If ya ever feel like doin' some comedy again, just let me know.
You'll usually find me 'round these parts. No more auditions for us, but that don't mean we can't practice our comedy routine together.
All right, Akihiko. Let's set course for the stars! We can talk over some joke ideas in the park over there!
Yeah! Let's ready up for the next audition!
